messages:
joe (Support): Hey ops, ACME reporting a sudden burst of 5xx / timeouts on hosted inference starting ~10:15 UTC. Customer saw many 504s and streaming cutoffs. Ticket C-3921. Can SRE take a look?

sam (ACME): saw ~18% error rate for ~20m. Traces show requests queued >8s, then gateway 504. No obvious client change on our end.

ana (SRE): taking. what's the tenant id?

joe (Support): tenant=acme-corp-19. P95 spiking to ~12s, p99 > 30s. Link to grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/ingress/hosted?orgId=1&from=now-30m

ana (SRE): grabbing metrics. Preliminary: continuous-batcher backlog for that tenant jumped at 10:12 UTC, dequeue rate stable but enqueue >> dequeue. KV cache eviction rate up 3x.

lina (ProdEng): that combo smells like prefix/KV churn: cache thrash causes batcher to stall while loading new keys -> backlog builds and we hit per-tenant queue depth limits, then gateway returns 504s.

ana (SRE): collecting traces and logs. Found repeated log lines from batcher: 

```
WARN batcher: load_prefixs: cache_miss=1.2k evict=230 load_ms=180
ERROR dequeue: tenant=acme-corp-19 enqueue_wait_ms=8200 queue_depth=415 limit=420
```

lina (ProdEng): interesting — queue_depth 415/420 -> near limit. We have a per-tenant soft limit at 420. If many long sequences come in, continuous batching holds entries in memory while waiting for batch formation; eviction thrash can extend wait.

ana (SRE): tried a replay against staging to reproduce: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{\"input\": \"ping\"}' https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate?model=open-lama` ran 2000 reqs in a loop and saw backlog form after ~150s. Attaching command used for repro.

jane (Support): deploy-bot shows a config rollout at 09:50 UTC that adjusted prefix pruning policy (smaller window). Could that increase cache miss rates?

deploy-bot: config-rollout: prefix-prune-window changed from 600s -> 90s at 09:50 UTC (rollback available).

lina (ProdEng): yep. Shorter prune window reduces memory use ordinarily but on this workload it increased thrash. Likely root cause: aggressive prune + a tenant with high variability -> KV churn -> batcher backlog -> queue depth hit -> gateway 5xx/504.

ana (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily raise per-tenant queue depth soft limit for hosted clusters from 420 -> 800 for affected hostpool, 2) revert prefix-prune-window to 600s for that rollout, 3) restart batcher workers gracefully to clear stuck entries.

lina (ProdEng): I'll push config revert and bump. Pushing hotfix to console config now.

lina (ProdEng): done. Reverted prefix-prune-window -> 600s and increased soft queue depth -> 800 for hostpool eu-west-1-a. Rolling restart scheduled.

ana (SRE): restart issued to batcher set for hostpool eu-west-1-a (drain, restart, uncordon).

joe (Support): relaying to ACME that we're applying a hotfix and will monitor.

~8 minutes later~

sam (ACME): confirmed errors dropped to <0.1% and streaming restored. Thanks.

ana (SRE): metrics look good. backlog subsided, p95 back to normal. I'll keep monitoring for 1h.

lina (ProdEng): follow-ups: add an alert for sustained KV eviction rate > 200/min correlated with tenant queue depth > 60% for 10m; add a runbook step to check recent config rollouts (prefix-prune changes). Also propose a safer default prune window for high-variability tenants.

joe (Support): customer updated ticket C-3921: service restored, will keep us posted.

ana (SRE): root cause summary (short): aggressive prefix-prune config change increased KV cache misses -> cache churn -> continuous-batcher stalls and backlog -> per-tenant queue soft limit hit -> gateway returned 504s/timeouts. Mitigation: revert prune window and raised soft depth + batcher restart. Next: alert + runbook + consider workload-based prune defaults.

lina (ProdEng): filing follow-up PR to change default and to add a canary gate for prune-window rollouts.

joe (Support): closing interim thread, moving to post-incident notes and runbook action items. :thumbsup:
